description:
Studying at university in Ireland has become the primary choice of many successful international students, thanks to both the prestigious job opportunities it offers to its students and the high-quality living conditions. While studying in Ireland, you not only get a high-quality education, but you also can improve your English.

The Technological University of Dublin is among the most important choices for students who want to study in Ireland, especially in the fields of engineering and science. The Technological University of Dublin is Ireland's first technological university, and although originally referred to as the Dublin Institute of Technology, it took its current name as of 1 January 2019. The school offers a wide variety of undergraduate programs, mainly in medicine, law, engineering, arts, and social sciences. TU Dublin has 5 campuses located in different parts of the city. The school has its main campus in the Grangegorman area, but also has long-term campuses in Tallaght and Blanchardstown. Today, the school is home to 29,700 students and includes students from 138 different nationalities. Accepting students from so many different nationalities, the school has become a favorite of international students in Ireland.

TU Dublin is ranked among the top 1000 universities in the world according to the best-known university rankings, QS World University Rankings and Times Higher Education Rankings. According to QS Rankings, the school's ranking for 2022 is 801. It ranked first among universities in Europe in terms of international student satisfaction.

Here are some of the popular undergraduate and graduate programs TU Dublin offers.

The greater Dublin area has a population of nearly 1.5 million people but the city centre itself is relatively small and easy to navigate. Each year, more than 100,000 students come to study in Dublin’s universities, colleges, and language schools, adding to the city’s vibrancy and to its increasingly cosmopolitan population. Over 28,000 TU Dublin students contribute to that vibrancy, studying on campuses that are in the city centre, and in the nearby suburbs of Blanchardstown and Tallaght. All are easily accessed by public transport and there is also lots of bike parking for students.
